I rechecked the current head `394e5e699fd88c2fd02f0e25970e23b0e7135340` against the QSV registration and probe code. One concrete Linux export failure remains; this review is based on source inspection only, without a local build or hardware run.

On non-Windows, `crates/platform/src/qsv/mod.rs` implements `probe_codec_hevc` as `IntelGpu::probe().ok().flatten().is_some()`, and `probe_codec_av1` as a device-ID range check. But `crates/platform/src/qsv/session.rs`'s non-Windows `QsvSession::new` always returns an error saying the Media Foundation path is Windows-only. `is_available()` and the HEVC/AV1 probes can therefore advertise Intel hardware encoding on Linux even though the only registered QSV factory cannot create a session. HEVC is reported available for any Intel device; AV1 is inferred from three hard-coded ID ranges. On such a system, the format can appear available, then the factory declines and export has no encoder.

Please make non-Windows QSV probes report unavailable until there is a working VA-API-backed session, or register a real Linux encoder whose capability checks match the formats and bit depths it can encode. Add a non-Windows regression that verifies the unavailable state (or exercises the working backend's probe-to-session path). I did not compile or execute this candidate.

dispositions.body: On the current head, this can still delete the selected timeline clip by accident. The new handling removes a selected effect or mask, but after that selection is cleared, a second Backspace matches neither branch and falls through to `edit.clear`. The same fallthrough occurs if Effect Controls has focus with no removable item selected. Please consume Clear and Ripple Delete whenever Effect Controls has focus, even when there is no target, and add regression coverage for both no selection and repeated Backspace after removing an effect or mask.

I found two unresolved import correctness issues in the current diff. First, the overlap recovery path calls `Builder::place(seq, kind, ti + 1, ...)` without enforcing `MAX_TRACKS`; an overlap at the last allowed XML track can create track 1000. Apply the same cap in this path and test overlap on the 999th track. Second, when placement returns `None`, the skipped clip remains in `xml_clip_ids` and `links`, so a later link-resolution/export path can treat a clip that was never imported as a real link member. Remove that clip's ID and pending link records on the skipped path, with a regression test that verifies no dangling/singleton link is produced.

The delayed-key-release case still disables the IME immediately. If `keys_down` remains true for a frame and the key-up arrives more than `HOLD` seconds after the last held-key frame, `since` already predates the hold interval; on the release frame `left <= 0` and the IME turns off. Track the transition from held to released and start the grace interval at the release time. Please add a test with a gap greater than `HOLD` before key-up and assert the IME remains active for the full grace period after release.

The current TTML parser still corrupts valid captions in two cases. It finds the first `>` even when that character is inside a quoted attribute value, so valid markup such as `text` can be split and lose its closing markup. It also trims whitespace between `<` and the tag name, so literal text such as `1 < b > 2` can be reinterpreted as markup and removed. Locate the tag terminator outside quoted values and require the tag name to start immediately after `<`; add parser/export round-trip tests for both cases. These are content-fidelity defects on untrusted caption text.

The playhead update only runs through the selected-clip branch. When Ripple Delete closes a selected gap, `ripple_delete_gap` returns before `cut_point` is calculated, so a playhead inside a gap from frame 48 to 96 remains at frame 72 after the gap closes. Please also move the playhead to the closed gap's start on successful selected-gap deletion and add a test with the playhead inside that gap. The existing selected-clip regression does not cover this separate path.

This does not type-check on non-macOS targets: `start_scrub` wraps `fill` in `Arc<Mutex<_>>` before the platform branch, then wraps it again inside the `#[cfg(not(target_os = "macos"))]` block. The worker therefore passes `Arc<Mutex<Arc<Mutex<Box<dyn FnMut...>>>>>` to `open`, which expects the single-wrapped callback type. Keep the initial wrapper macOS-only or restructure the shared type so the non-macOS worker receives exactly one `Arc<Mutex<Fill>>`. Please verify the fix with Windows and Linux `cargo check`/hosted builds; the platform-specific code is otherwise invisible to a macOS-only compile.

The updated whitespace handling preserves non-breaking and other Unicode spaces, but `clean` still trims leading/trailing XML whitespace around the assembled cue and `str::lines()` drops a final line break. Since `
` is represented as `\n`, cues beginning or ending with a break lose that authored line break (for example `


text

` and `

text

`). Please preserve intentional edge breaks while normalizing XML whitespace, and add round-trip tests for both leading and trailing `
` cases.

The non-finite recovery sweep still leaves `DeReverb`'s recursive PSD state poisoned. In the changed frame callback, `psd = alpha * st.psd[k] + (1.0 - alpha) * p` is stored whenever `psd < 1e-30` is false; for NaN that comparison is false, so NaN is written to both `st.psd[k]` and its history ring. Later finite frames keep the PSD non-finite, and the `st.psd[k] > 0.0` test selects unity gain, bypassing the intended reverb reduction. Clear non-finite PSD values as well as tiny values, then strengthen the recovery test to assert DeReverb's gain reduction recovers after a bad sample, not only that its output becomes finite.

The paired FFT path lets a non-finite sample in one channel contaminate its clean neighbor. `analyse_pair` packs frames as `a + i*b`; an input NaN/Inf propagates through the complex FFT, and the split produces non-finite bins for both channels before both are synthesized. The previous independent-channel path kept this failure isolated. Before using `analyse_pair`, detect non-finite samples in either frame and process the channels independently for that frame (or use another isolation-preserving path). Please add symmetric bad-left/clean-right and clean-left/bad-right regression tests that assert the unaffected channel remains finite. This is a recovery correctness issue for untrusted audio, not a rounding-parity tolerance issue.

`Language::Lo` is now selectable and can be loaded from saved or system-locale preferences, but this PR adds no Lao font fallback or availability guard. The existing `cjk::install` path only supplies Chinese and Korean faces; on systems without a Lao-capable default font, choosing Lao can render the interface as missing-glyph boxes, and startup/locale selection has no way to fall back to English or tell the user why. Please add coverage-based Lao system-font discovery and installation (or a correctly licensed bundled face), expose availability, guard manual selection and both saved/system preferences, and test the unavailable-font fallback. The catalog itself is not sufficient to make the interface usable without a glyph source.

This PR's patch no longer reaches the active Matroska parser on current `main`. The PR is based on `abf44fd`, but current `main` has removed `crates/matroska/src/demux.rs`; `crates/matroska/src/lib.rs` is now a thin re-export of `craft_media::matroska`, and FilmCraft pins `craft-media` from `storytold/craft-libs`. The ms-rounded fix works for the case in #1700, but the new rate estimate gets a simpler case wrong, and two other changes are unexplained. I'm requesting changes.

**A 30 fps clip with one dropped frame is now read as 29.97.** `frame_rate_from_durations` first takes the mean (`mp4.rs:678-695`) and accepts the closest common rate within 1.5 %. The old code took the median, which was exactly 3000 units for these files. Take a 90 kHz track with 3000-unit frames and one 6000-unit gap (a dropped frame):
- in 100 samples the mean is 29.70 fps, which is 0.89 % from 29.97 and 0.99 % from 30, so the closest common rate is 29.97;
- in the 240-sample window the function uses, the mean is 29.88 fps and the closest is still 29.97.

The modal-duration fallback is only reached when the mean is more than 1.5 % from every rate, so it never runs here. A frame rate that is 0.1 % off is what makes New Sequence From Clip drop a frame every 33 seconds, which is the symptom in #1700. Your VFR test uses a gap every seventh frame (`rounded_pts_tests.rs:206-210`), so it can't see this. Please use the median or modal duration first (accepted when it is within the timescale's rounding of a common rate), and fall back to the mean only when that fails, and add a test with a single dropped frame in 120.

**Changes requested: pasting into a different graphic can re-target a pin to an unrelated layer.**
`adopt_layer_copies` decides whether a pin to a layer that wasn't copied survives by looking at the destination's uids: `None if !present.contains(&u) => extra.pin = None, None => {}`, and the description says "a pin to a layer the destination does not have is dropped". And `PinTarget::Layer(uid)` is resolved only inside the owning clip (`nodes.iter().position(|m| m.uid == uid && uid != 0)` in `graphic_design.rs`). I read the DSP (`remix.rs`, `remix_levels.rs`), `crates/render/src/remix.rs`, `crates/engine/src/remix.rs`, `crates/edit/src/lib.rs` (`clamp_trim`), `crates/project/src/lib.rs` (`remix_output_duration`) and the Timeline waveform and splice code against main. I haven't built or run it (no cargo here). I'm requesting one change, because the new level matching can make a remix fail that works on main.

**Changes requested: a remix with more than 33 pieces now fails to plan.**
`make_plan` (`crates/engine/src/remix.rs`) turns the result of `dsp::match_levels` into a hard error: `.ok_or_else(|| EngineError::Other("cannot read audio for remix level matching".into()))?`. `match_levels` returns `None` for `plan.pieces.len() > 33`, and also when any one of its reads fails (the `read(...)?` calls). But `dsp::plan` has no limit on pieces: `joints_for(segments)` gives 1–3 joints, and the loop `while (target - len) / k > max_span * 0.9 && target / (k + 2) >= min_piece { k += 1 }` keeps adding joints as the target grows (the doc comment says "more when a long extension needs them"). By my reading, at 120 bpm a 30-second loop needs 33 joints once the target passes roughly 13 minutes (`max_span` = 30 s − 2 × 2 s = 26 s, × 0.9 = 23.4 s per joint, so `k` reaches 33 when `(target − 30) / 32 > 23.4`), and a 60-second track at roughly 28 minutes. On main both plan fine, since nothing caps pieces there (`git grep 33` finds nothing in the remix plan code on main); on this head, Remix Properties on such a clip returns "cannot read audio for remix level matching" and the remix is refused. The same 33-piece limit is also applied in `remix_output_duration` (so the Out-trim fix doesn't apply) and in `draw_remix_splices` (no markers), which degrade quietly, but those are the only places that do.

`Remix::levels` is already an `Option`, and `render_with_levels(..., None, ...)` is byte-for-byte the old render (the envelope and correlation terms are only applied for `Some`), so the fallback exists: when `match_levels` returns `None`, keep `levels: None` (and, if you want, say so in the status) instead of failing the remix. Or raise the cap and the `from_text` and `remix_output_duration` limits consistently with what `plan` can produce. A test that plans a long extension of a short track and checks it still succeeds would pin it.
